text:
lina: ACME-prod hitting sudden p95 spikes and intermittent 429s on a Dedicated eu-west pool (ded-eu1-gpu-pool-17). Started ~2026-03-16T10:04Z, autoscale didn't seem to protect them. Suspect noisy neighbor / MIG contention. Any quick triage?

alex: Can you drop the autoscale events and the p95 timeline? Also any auth/billing anomalies reported by the tenant?

lina: Paste of recent autoscale events and metric snippet: 
```
autoscale.events:
2026-03-16T10:03:48Z scale_up_req id=ae23 status=THROTTLED(reason=pool_capacity_fractional)
2026-03-16T10:05:59Z scale_up_req id=ae24 status=SUCCESS
2026-03-16T10:06:30Z scale_down id=ae20 status=SUCCESS

metrics:
p95_latency: 2026-03-16T09:58 1.2s -> 10:04 3.7s -> 10:08 1.4s
429_rate: peaked 8/min at 10:05
billing.alert: unusual token burst coincident with latency spike
```

ops-bot: alert: [DED_POOL:ded-eu1-gpu-pool-17] tenant=acme-prod p95_latency>3s and 429_rate>5/min (2026-03-16T10:05:10Z) :eyes: 

ben-sre: Can we get node-level telemetry from the nodes hosting acme's slices? Particularly MIG layout and nvidia stats (SM, memory bw) for last 10m. Any eviction logs?

zoe: grabbing node logs now, quick snippet from node-17 (cohost node) at 10:04:
```
node-17 nvidia-smi mig -lgi
GPU 0: MIG profiles active: [1g.5gb, 1g.5gb, 2g.10gb]
10:04:12 SM util (slice 0/1/2): 95% / 8% / 7%
10:04:12 Memory BW: slice0=92% slice1=12% slice2=14%
scheduler: co-located small slices packed onto same GPU for throughput
kernel logs: kworker: high preempt on gpu driver, ctx-switch spikes
```

zoe: Also noticed many small requests from a different tenant on slice0 showing continuous KV cache churn. That aligns with high SM utilization and our p95 jumps.

alex: Hypothesis: mixed MIG profiles in same physical GPU means heavy tenant got placed into a 1g slice and saturated SM/BW causing other fractional slices to starve; autoscaler saw fractional capacity accounted and initial scale_up was throttled (reason=pool_capacity_fractional) until a full slot became free, causing a short window of 429s.

lina: Customer also mentioned a token refresh error earlier (brief 401s) around 10:02; they blamed client but timing overlaps. Could be that their retries exacerbated load.

ben-sre: Repro steps I'm going to run: 
```
1) create a mixed-profile dedicated node (1g.5gb x2 + 2g.10gb x1)
2) run a steady KV-cache-heavy workload against one 1g slice (high SM) and a bursty inference workload on the 2g slice
3) observe SM/mem BW contention and autoscale decision logs
4) check scale_up throttle reason and quota accounting for fractional MIG slots
```

alex: Immediate mitigations: 1) Move acme-prod off the shared node to an isolated slice (temp fix), 2) bump their autoscale policy to allow quicker scale_up (short-term), 3) schedule a rolling migration to a homogeneous pool. Longer-term: make the scheduler MIG-aware so it avoids packing heavy+light slices on same GPU, and surface per-MIG capacity accounting in autoscale decisions and billing.

zoe: I'll attach node logs and nvlink traces to the ticket and run the repro on a staging pool tonight.

lina: Thanks — I'll notify the customer about temporary migration and the ETA for the more permanent fix. :thumbsup:

ben-sre: tagging eng-runtime and sched-team for visibility. filing esk:ENG-4319.

ops-bot: ticket ENG-4319 created and linked to alert ded-eu1-gpu-pool-17.

alex: Good call. Also add a metric that tracks per-MIG throttles so we can alert earlier.

zoe: noted. I'll follow up with a short runbook for support: how to identify mixed-MIG noisy neighbor and quick isolation steps.

lina: cool — closing loop after migration is confirmed.
